Manual QA · real-user session · two passes

OneCAD Modeling UX Review

A full pass over the sketching and modeling tools of the real desktop app, driven the way a person drives it — physical pointer and keyboard against the live Tauri window, the Rust runtime and the OCCT worker. Every finding was then re-run from a cold start in a second, independent session and photographed. Benchmarked against Shapr3D.

Date
14 September 2026
Sessions
2 · cold start each
Fidelity
real_user · cgevent
Actions
291 · 6 diagnostic
Findings
59
Failed to reproduce
0

The surface craft is good. Status hints, disabled-tool reasons, the trim preview, the feature-edit preview and the snap-settings panel all read like a product with taste behind it.

Underneath, the two things a parametric CAD has to get right are currently wrong. The constraint solver reports a clean sketch on geometry that violates its own constraints. And a sketch drawn on a face does not follow that face when the parent feature changes, producing a silently wrong model — no banner, no repair state, a regen log that says failedSteps=0 needsRepair=0.

The most ordinary sketching actions each end badly: drawing a rectangle with the Line tool yields a conflicting sketch, dragging a corner does nothing and corrupts the constraint set, filleting a corner makes the profile unusable, trimming a circle silently deletes its diameter. Grid snapping — on by default, with an on-screen badge announcing it — does not snap. And a 3D fillet is in practice unreachable, because clicking an edge selects the adjoining face instead.

8Blocking correctness
15Snapping & sketch feedback

23Naming, copy & chrome
Second-pass verification. The whole flow was rebuilt from a new project in a second session, with a screenshot captured for each finding at the moment it occurred.
  • 52 of 56 first-pass findings were re-run and all 52 reproduced. None failed to reproduce.
  • 4 could not be re-reached in the second session — the fillet-panel naming items (N3, N4, N8) and N10 — because the new defect T8 makes an edge selection practically impossible. They stand on first-pass evidence and are marked as such.
  • 4 were revised in detail once better evidence was available: S3, V2, T2, T3. The revisions are stated inside each finding.
  • 3 new findings surfaced during verification: S15, T8, N12.
  • Two loose first-pass impressions were dropped rather than promoted: "orbit also changes the camera distance" did not reproduce (orbit ran at ~0.55°/px with no distance change), and "the viewport has no hover pre-highlight" is wrong — faces do highlight on hover; only edges do not, which is T8.

01 Correctness — blocking

Each of these produces a wrong model or an unusable sketch from an ordinary sequence of actions. Fix before anything below.

B1Blockingreproduced
A-259 · A-262
A-264 · A-273
log rev 22

A sketch on a face does not follow the face; the dependent cut silently does nothing

Extrude a profile 40 mm, select the top face, sketch a rectangle on it, extrude-cut 15 mm down. Then re-edit the first Extrude from 40 mm to 25 mm.

The body shrinks — but the sketch plane stays at Z = 40, floating in mid-air above the new top face. The cut that depends on it now starts 15 mm above the material and reaches exactly Z = 25, so it removes nothing and leaves only an imprint of the rectangle on the top face. History still lists the feature as completed. The regen log calls the run clean:

regen: published … steps=5 changed=1 removed=0 failedSteps=0 needsRepair=0   (rev 22)

No repair banner, no NeedsRepair, no diagnostic. The status bar says "New body created" (see N9). In the first session, undoing back to 40 mm restored the pocket, which confirms the chain is otherwise intact.

Shapr3D — a sketch made on a face moves with the face.

B2Blockingreproduced
A-183 · A-184
(diagnostic)

The solver reports a clean sketch while its constraints are violated

After removing one redundant constraint from a closed four-line loop, the inspector reads Under-constrained · DOF 3 with an empty conflict set. A diagnostic read of the same session shows the geometry does not satisfy the constraints listed as active:

ConstraintEntityResidual (second pass)First pass
c1 Horizontale1ΔY = 0.000 mm ✓1.396 mm
c3 Verticale2ΔX = 1.082 mm1.047 mm
c5 Horizontale3ΔY = 1.431 mm1.431 mm
c8 Verticale4ΔX = 0.906 mm0.953 mm

Side lengths came out 80 / 62 / 82 / 63.43 mm — impossible for a closed loop whose four sides are all horizontal or vertical. The user sees a rectangle, the inspector says the sketch is healthy, and the extruded solid is a skewed prism.

The likely cause is that deleting a constraint does not trigger a re-solve and the status is recomputed without checking residuals. Whatever the cause, a "clean" status that does not imply satisfied constraints is worse than no status at all.

B3Blockingreproduced
A-182 · A-183
A-210 (contrast)

Drawing a rectangle with the Line tool produces a conflicting sketch out of the box

Four clicks to close a rectangular loop, accepting every auto-inferred constraint, ends in Conflicting · DOF 2 — Conflicting constraints. Remove one to resolve. Auto-inference applies Perpendicular on top of Horizontal/Vertical on the same pairs, so the set is redundant. Deleting one Perpendicular cleared the conflict immediately, in both sessions.

The Rectangle tool produces a clean set from the same shape — 4 Coincident, 2 Horizontal, 2 Vertical, 2 Distance, no conflict. So the defect is the Line tool's inference, not the solver.

The error also names no culprit: all eleven constraint rows turn red at once and the user is told to "remove one" with no indication which.

B4Blockingreproduced
A-222 · A-223
new region hash

A 2D fillet makes the sketch unusable as a profile

Rectangle → circle → trim → 2D fillet on one corner → Finish sketch produces a red status-bar error:

Sketch not usable as a profile: opFailed: op failed (OpFailed, recoverable=true):
finishSketch: SketchRegions: incomplete triangulation for region r_b05fd1d21f09c4f2

The second session produced a different region hash from the first (r_698b0a5a3cd6e631), which rules out a one-off and confirms the failure is deterministic for this shape. Arming Extrude fails the same way. Deleting the fillet arc and re-finishing succeeds with no error, which isolates the 2D fillet as the cause.

B5Blockingreproduced
A-227 · A-229

Deleting a 2D fillet leaves the profile open

The two trimmed lines are not extended back to their intersection, so the loop has a visible gap and Extrude reports Regions: 0. Between this and B4 the user has no way out of a filleted corner.

Shapr3D and Fusion — both restore the corner when the fillet is removed.

B6Blockingreproduced
A-186

Dragging a vertex of a closed rectangle fails and corrupts the sketch

A left-drag of a corner moved nothing, reported "Snap target not reached; the solver kept the geometry at its solved position", and flipped the sketch from Under-constrained · DOF 3 to Conflicting · DOF 3 with three constraints marked red. The conflict persists after release. Identical in both sessions, down to the hint text.

Shapr3D — direct manipulation of under-constrained geometry is a primary interaction. Here it neither works nor fails safely.

B7Blockingreproduced
A-215 → A-218

Trim silently discards dimensions

Trimming the circle removed both its Diameter 25 mm and its Midpoint constraint; DOF went 4 → 9 with no warning. The user's explicit dimension is simply gone.

Shapr3D — keeps the radius dimension on the trimmed arc.

B8Highreproduced
A-220

2D fillet adds no radius dimension

Filleting a corner at 5 mm added two Coincident constraints and nothing else; DOF went 9 → 14. The radius the user typed is never captured, so it cannot be edited afterwards.

02 Snapping and sketch feedback

The area the brief asked to focus on, and the area where the gap to Shapr3D is widest. Snapping partly works; almost none of it is legible to the user.

S1Blockingreproduced
A-171 · A-172
A-173

Grid snapping does not snap

Grid snap on, grid 20 mm, snap radius M. The second pass settled this with an adjacent-pixel probe: moving the cursor 2 px changed the readout from U −46.00 to U −44.97 — continuous motion of 0.515 mm per pixel, with no step and no lock. Clicking then places the point at exactly the unsnapped coordinate.

The Grid badge is displayed the whole time. It advertises a snap that never happens. Wire it up or stop showing it.

S2Highreproduced
A-212 → A-215

The snap badge names the wrong snap

Hovering the midpoint of an edge shows On Curve. Committing there creates a Midpoint constraint. So point snapping does work and produces the right constraint — but the badge never says which snap is engaged. Across both sessions the only label ever shown near existing geometry was On Curve: for edge interiors, midpoints and near-corners alike.

Shapr3D — names the snap it is about to take. That label is the entire contract between the user and the snapping engine; a generic one is close to useless.

S3Highrevised
A-181

Closing a loop happens silently — no endpoint highlight, no badge, no snapped readout

Revised after the second pass. The first pass concluded there was no endpoint snap at all. That was too strong: clicking 2.2 mm from the open endpoint does close the loop and create the Coincident. What is missing is every piece of feedback around it — approaching the endpoint produces no badge, no highlight on the target, and a readout that shows the raw unsnapped cursor coordinates right up to the click.

The user cannot tell whether they are about to close a loop or leave a 2 mm gap. Given that leaving a gap costs them a whole extrude (see B5), that is the wrong thing to leave invisible.

S4Highreproduced
A-174 · A-181
A-207 · A-218

The snap badge is stale and sticky

The badge renders where an earlier hover left it and stays there. In the second pass the Grid badge acquired at A-171 was still in the same place at A-181 — through a 160 px cursor move, four clicks and three committed segments. It survives Escape, and on the face sketch the stale On Curve badge sat on top of the 30 mm dimension label for the rest of the session.

S5Highreproduced
both sessions,
never rendered

No inference guide lines, ever

Sketch guide lines and Sketch guide points are both on in snap settings, yet no dashed alignment guide was rendered at any point in either session — not when drawing nearly vertically below an existing point, not when approaching an endpoint, not when aligning to the origin.

Shapr3D — dashed inference guides are how a user understands why a point landed where it did. Without them the snapping is invisible even when it works (see S2).

A-206 → A-207

Typed values do not appear until the mouse moves

Typing 30 with the Rectangle tool armed left the chip reading H 0 mm and the focus target still non-editable. The value had been buffered — moving the mouse one pixel revealed W 30 already entered. A user types, sees nothing happen, and types again.

S7Mediumreproduced

vs A-119

Sketch tools have no live preview of a typed dimension

Typing a length in the Line tool, or W/H in the Rectangle tool, does not update the rubber band — the preview keeps following the cursor until Enter. Extrude and 3D Fillet do update live, and it is markedly better. Make the sketch tools match.

S8Mediumreproduced
A-176

Tab in the Line tool wipes the typed value

Rectangle and Circle document Tab as the second field (width → height, diameter → radius) and it works. In the Line tool, which has only a length, Tab clears the field instead of being ignored. Silent data loss on a key the adjacent tools teach you to press.

S9Mediumreproduced
A-212 · A-218

Chips and labels stack on top of each other

The snap badge, the live-dimension chip and the existing 30 mm dimension label all render at the same spot and overlap. In the second session the stale On Curve badge sat directly on the 30 mm label from the trim onward.

S10Mediumreproduced
A-182

Constraints are anonymous, and conflicts name no culprit

The list is eleven rows reading Coincident, Coincident, Horizontal, Perpendicular, … with no entity names, no numbering, and no way to tell two Coincidents apart. On a conflict every row turns red at once. The rows are not focusable, so only hover reveals anything — and the hover label was itself stale in the first session.

S11Mediumreproduced
A-188

Contradictory status vocabulary

After an undo the panel read Over-constrained · DOF 3 — Sketch is over-constrained. Remove or change a conflicting constraint. Over-constrained and three remaining degrees of freedom are mutually exclusive to a reader. The three states (Under-constrained / Over-constrained / Conflicting) also do not map onto a single axis, so the badge is hard to read at a glance.

S12Mediumreproduced
A-189

Selecting a sketch entity shows no properties

Clicking a line selected it and surfaced a two-icon unlabeled context chip, but the inspector did not change — no length, no endpoints, no coordinates, no radius for an arc.

S13Mediumreproduced
A-224

Re-opening a sketch arms the Line tool

Double-clicking a sketch in the tree enters it with Line active, not Select. One stray click adds geometry to a sketch you only meant to inspect.

S14Lowreproduced
A-220 vs A-224
A-050 · A-164

Smaller sketch-feedback items

  • The constraint list comes back in a different order after re-opening the same sketch, so positional memory is useless.
  • Coincident badges default to off, so the constraint that most often explains "why can't I move this" is invisible.
  • Snap-settings naming is abstract where CAD has conventional words: "Sketch guide points" covers endpoint, midpoint and centre, while "Quadrant points" and "Intersections" use the conventional names.
  • Select mode has no status hint at all; every other tool has a good one.
S15NewA-207

Live dimension chips mix precisions in the same pair

While drawing a rectangle the two chips read W 30 mm and H 16.225 mm at the same moment — one integer, one to three decimals. Every other chip in the app rounds to whole millimetres. Pick a display precision and apply it consistently, or the numbers read as noise.

03 Viewport and camera

Orbit, pan and wheel zoom themselves are fine — orbit runs at roughly 0.55°/px, the wheel classified correctly as a mouse, and the navigation-help popover is accurate. The defaults are the problem.

V1Highreproduced
A-157

The default camera is a poor first impression

A new project opens in perspective at FOV 76° with the camera almost in the ground plane. The grid is extremely foreshortened, the horizon sits a fifth of the way down the window, and a box does not look like a box. Switching the same model to Ortho is dramatically more legible.

Open in an isometric three-quarter view, drop the default FOV to roughly 30–35°, and consider Ortho as the default for a CAD tool.

V2Mediumrevised
A-201 · A-264

Zoom to fit does not centre the model

Revised after the second pass. The first pass described the fit as "edge to edge, under the chrome". Measured properly in the second session, the real behaviour is an off-centre fit: after ⇧F the body sat 63 px from the left edge and 267 px from the right, and low in the frame. The likely cause is that the fit box includes the origin triad and datum markers rather than just the visible bodies.

Fix both halves: fit to the visible geometry, and inset the fit rect by the floating toolbar and inspector so the result is centred in the usable area with ~10 % padding.

V3Mediumreproduced
A-203

Entering a sketch on a face zooms too tight

The projected face fills the viewport corner to corner — 41 px of margin on the left and none at the top — so there is no room to draw outside it or to see the surrounding body. The opaque teal region fill also hides the 3D context entirely, and two of the projected-edge lock badges overlap each other at the right edge.

V4Mediumreproduced
A-170

The TOP view of the XY plane is rotated

In a sketch on XY viewed from TOP, screen-right is +Y (green) and screen-down is +X (red). The conventional top view is X right, Y up; sketch U/V then does not correspond to X/Y either, which makes the status-bar readout hard to reason about.

V5Lowreproduced
A-279 · A-290

The coordinate readout does not blank outside the viewport

With the cursor parked in the left sidebar the status bar still reported X −32.25 Y −64.26 Z 0.00 mm; with the cursor over the toolbar it reported X −411.18. The numbers are stale and meaningless whenever the pointer is not over the 3D view.

04 Tool chips and operations

The operation HUD is a good idea executed a few degrees off: it sits where you need to click, and its most consequential control is unlabelled. And one new blocker surfaced during verification — edges cannot be picked.

T8NewBlockingA-266 · A-267
A-271 · A-272
A-287 · A-289

Edges cannot be picked, so Fillet / Chamfer is unreachable

Five clicks aimed at three different silhouette edges, at 1–3 px accuracy, every one selected the adjoining face instead. Hovering an edge produces no pre-highlight at all, while hovering a face does highlight it — so there is no visual feedback to aim with, and no way to tell you are on the edge before you commit.

There is no alternative entry point. Fillet / Chamfer is disabled when a face is selected and disabled when a whole body is selected; it only enables for an edge. (Shell is likewise disabled with a body selected.) A user who cannot hit an edge cannot fillet at all.

The first session did select an edge successfully on the first attempt at a different camera angle, so this is inconsistent rather than impossible — which makes it worse to live with, not better.

T1Highreproduced
A-243 · A-244
A-245

The tool chip covers the geometry it asks you to click, and eats the click

With Extrude armed the chip floats directly over the sketch profile. A click aimed at the profile but landing on the chip was silently swallowed — the count stayed 0 regions and, worse, the click fell through to the body's top face and highlighted it, so the user gets feedback for something they did not intend. Clicking 72 px to the left picked the region immediately.

The chip has a Dock affordance, which suggests this is known, but the default position is wrong and a swallowed click needs feedback.

T2Highrevised
A-192 · A-194
A-195

The ↔ in the Extrude panel is "Symmetric", and nothing on screen says so

Revised after the second pass. The control is not unlabelled in the markup — it carries aria-label="Symmetric" and title="Symmetric (hold Alt while dragging)". But neither ever reaches a sighted user: there is no visible label, and a deliberate 3-second hover produced no tooltip at all. The app's own instant tooltip system, used on the main toolbar, is not wired to this control, and the native title tooltip does not render in this WebView.

So the only thing on screen is a double-headed arrow next to a direction-dependent operation, which reads as "flip". In the first session that produced a committed feature with Symmetric: Yes when a one-way cut was intended. Give it a visible label and route it through the app's tooltip system.

T3Mediumrevised
A-248

There is no direction control; reversing means dragging into negative numbers

Revised after the second pass. The first pass said there was no way to reverse an extrude. There is one: drag the depth handle back through zero and the value goes negative (−16.3 mm), which is what actually reverses the cut. But nothing tells you that, the arrow does not flip to a positive value, and there is no button for it — so the discoverable-looking control (T2) is the wrong one and the working one is undocumented.

T4Mediumreproduced
A-247

The Cut preview turns the entire body bright red

Red-on-everything reads as an error state rather than "this will subtract". Tint the removed volume and leave the target body neutral.

T5Lowreproduced
A-248 · A-252

Direction: Normal [0, 0, 1] never updates

It still read [0, 0, 1] while the preview was cutting downward at −16.3 mm, and again after the feature committed at −15 mm.

T6Mediumreproduced
A-255 vs A-192

Re-editing an Extrude hides half its options

In feature-edit mode the panel shows only the draft-angle field. Blind / Through all / To next / To face and New Body / Add / Cut are both gone, so an extrude cannot be changed from Add to Cut after the fact.

T7Lowreproduced
A-196

Inconsistent rounding between the drag handle and sketch dimensions

Dragging the extrude depth handle produced 45.93 mm with no rounding, while Dimension rounding is on by default for sketches. Pick one policy.

07 What already works well

All re-confirmed in the second session. Worth protecting through the fixes above.

Trim hover preview

Target segment red, the rest cyan. Exactly right, and the clearest interaction in the app.

Feature-edit preview

Solid below the new height, ghosted above, plus the honest hint "Approximate feature-edit preview; final geometry updates on Apply".

Face-sketch projection

The host face's edges auto-project into a new sketch with lock badges, and the inspector says "4 projected reference edges · draw geometry to begin".

Disabled tools explain themselves

"Select a sketch region (or a sketch) to extrude" — better than most CAD.

Per-tool status hints

Genuinely useful throughout, and they teach the numeric-entry and Tab conventions.

Rectangle, Circle, Measure

Clean constraint sets, working Tab-to-second-field, and a correct on-canvas area label.

Snap settings panel

Unusually rich for a young app, including the Alt-to-place-freely note.

Topological re-binding

The fillet re-bound correctly to the new edge after the parent extrude changed height — the part of the identity system that is working.

08 Suggested order of work

Grouped by what each band buys. The first band is correctness; the second is the sketching feel a Shapr3D comparison is really about.

Fix before anything else
1B1Sketch-on-face must follow its host face, and a cut that removes nothing must not report success. This is the project's stated reason for existing.
2B2Never report a clean status on geometry that violates its constraints. Re-solve after a constraint is deleted, and gate the status on residuals.
3T8Make edges pickable: give them a hover pre-highlight, a screen-space pick radius that beats the adjoining face, and enable Fillet / Chamfer from a face or body selection as a fallback.
4B3Stop the Line tool emitting Perpendicular alongside Horizontal/Vertical.
5B4 · B52D fillet must produce a triangulable region, and deleting one must restore the corner.
6S1Make grid snapping snap, or remove the badge.
Then — the sketching feel
7S2 · S5Name the snap in the badge — End, Mid, Centre, On curve, Grid, Intersection — and draw the dashed inference guide that explains it. Together these are most of the perceived quality gap.
8S3Highlight the endpoint you are about to snap to, and show the snapped coordinate rather than the raw cursor, so closing a loop is visible before the click.
9S4 · S9Clear the snap badge when the snap ends, anchor it to the cursor, and stop chips stacking on dimension labels.
10B6Dragging under-constrained geometry must work, and must never leave a conflict behind.
11B7 · B8Trim must preserve dimensions; 2D fillet must create a radius dimension.
12S6 · S7 · S8 · S15Typed dimensions should render immediately, preview live, keep one precision, and Tab must never destroy input.
Then — clarity
13S10 · S11Name constraints by their entities, point at the actual conflict, and settle on one status vocabulary.
14N1 · N2Add a user-facing error layer. Never show enum names, flags or region hashes, and never let an error reflow the status bar.
15T1 · T2 · T4Move the tool chip off the pick target and give feedback when it eats a click; give the Symmetric toggle a visible label and a working tooltip; stop painting the whole body red on a cut.
16V1 · V2 · V3A sane default camera, a fit that centres on the visible bodies inside the usable area, and breathing room when entering a face sketch.
17N3–N12 · C1–C11Naming and chrome consistency.

Evidence and method

Two sessions, each starting from a cold app launch and a brand-new project. Every interaction cited is mode: real_user, backend: cgevent — physical OS pointer and keyboard input against the real window — with two exceptions. The Edit ▸ Undo invocations ran through the app menu (mode: accessibility), deliberately, because this machine's Slovak keyboard layout swaps the positional Z and Y keys and would send the wrong chord. Six reads are marked diagnostic; they dump sketch geometry from window.__stores to obtain the exact residuals behind B2. Every screenshot on this page is a native window capture taken at the moment the finding occurred, and the user-visible proof for every finding is a screenshot, a status-bar message, or a dev.jsonl line.

Exercised: new project · sketch on a base plane (Line, numeric entry, auto-constraints, closing a loop) · finish sketch · Extrude (drag handle, typed depth, New Body / Add / Cut, negative depth) · face selection · sketch on a face (Rectangle, Circle, Trim, 2D Fillet, delete) · extrude cut · 3D Fillet (first session) · history feature edit and regen · undo · Measure · command palette · Save As (native panel) · snap settings · orbit, pan, wheel zoom, fit, home, front, ortho · tooltips and status hints.

Not exercised: Revolve, Shell, Hole, patterns, Mirror, Move, Datum plane, Combine, Section view, Variables, Library, export, and save-to-disk completion with reopen — the Save As panel was opened and verified, then cancelled so that no file was written to the machine. No existing project or autosave entry was opened.

Both sessions ended with session_stop reporting survivors: [] and ports 1420 and 4445 free. The full report with per-finding reproduction steps is committed at docs/qa/UX_REVIEW_2026-09-14.md; the raw capture set is under .tauri-agent/artifacts/s-20260914-195854-f4d4/.
